## Data Science at the Command Line

This example demonstrates how quarto-term can be used to write
tutorials about command-line data processing — similar to
[Data Science at the Command Line](https://datascienceatthecommandline.com).

### Creating Sample Data

```{term}
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/data.csv
name,age,city
Alice,30,New York
Bob,25,San Francisco
Charlie,35,Chicago
Diana,28,Boston
Eve,32,Seattle
EOF
cat /tmp/data.csv
```

### Exploring with Standard Tools

Count lines (including header):

```{term}
wc -l < /tmp/data.csv
```

Extract just the names:

```{term}
cut -d, -f1 /tmp/data.csv | tail -n +2
```

### Sorting and Filtering

Sort by age:

```{term}
sort -t, -k2 -n /tmp/data.csv | tail -n +2
```

Find people over 30:

```{term}
awk -F, 'NR>1 && $2>30 {print $1, $2}' /tmp/data.csv
```

### Piping It All Together

Get the oldest person's city:

```{term}
sort -t, -k2 -nr /tmp/data.csv | head -1 | cut -d, -f3
```

### Cleanup

```{term}
rm -f /tmp/data.csv
```
